sentences.text: Magistrate for Exclusive Trial of CCB (Relating to Cheating Cases in Chennai) and CBCID Metro Cases at Egmore, Chennai.

2. The case of the petitioner is that based on the complaint given by one Babu who is the partner of M/s.Vignesh & Co., the case in Crime No.296 of 2020 was registered for the offence under Section 420 and 406 IPC as against A1 and A2 in which, A1 is a company namely M/s.Merck Automobiles Private Limited and A2/Sudhakaran is the husband of the petitioner herein.

Thereafter, on completion of investigation, the respondent police filed the final report by showing the petitioner as A3 for the offences under Sections 420 and 406 IPC read with Section 34 IPC and the same was taken on file in C.C. No.202 of 2022 by the learned Metropolita Magistrate for Exclusive Trial of CCB https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (Relating to Cheating Cases in Chennai) and CBCID Metro Cases at Egmore, Chennai.
Therefore, the petitioner filed a petition before the Magistrate under Section 239 of Cr.P.C. in Crl.M.P.No.34096 of 2023 seeking to discharge her from the said case.
However, the learned Magistrate dismissed the same by order dated 22.10.2024.
Hence, the present petition is filed.
3. The contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner/A3 is the non- participating Director of A1-Company and she did not involve herself in the day to day affairs of the A1-Company.
Only A2 who is the Managing Director of A1 Company was dealing with the day to day affairs of A1-Company.
Even defacto complainant gave the complaint only as against A2 and not against the petitioner/A3.
Further, the said cheques were signed by A2 as signatory of A1- Company.

4. Heard both sides and perused the materials available on record.
5.
Though the petitioner is one of the Directors of the A1-Company, there is no material to show that the petitioner/A3 also involved in the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis commission of offence.

All the allegations and materials are only against A2.
6.

Since there is no prima facie material to proceed as against the petitioner/A3, the order dated 22.10.2024 passed in Crl.M.P.No.34096 of 2024 in Calendar Case No.202 of 2022 by the learned Metropolita Magistrate for Exclusive Trial of CCB (Relating to Cheating Cases in Chennai) and CBCID Metro Cases at Egmore, Chennai, is set aside.

Consequently, the Calendar Case No.202 of 2022 on the file of the Metropolitan Magistrate for Exclusive Trial of CCB (Relating to Cheating Cases in Chennai) and CBCID Metro Cases at Egmore, Chennai, is quashed as against the petitioner herein alone.
7. Accordingly, this Criminal Original Petition is allowed.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
